# `gear.gdl` is the manifest a role is declared in, and the runtime is not what refuses to honour it

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-role-qualified-names`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

Two documents have been describing the same construct from opposite ends, and
neither names the other.

### What ADR-0009 decides, and the half it leaves open

`cpt-cf-adr-instance-addressable-discovery` (accepted, 2026-08-06) decides how a
gear that runs in differentiated **roles** is reached. Its modelling rule:

> **Roles -> distinct directory names (manifest-declared).** When a gear runs in
> differentiated **roles** (front-door vs internal, or genuinely different
> contracts), each role registers under its **own directory name**. The gear
> stays **one gear** (one binary, one `deps`, mode-selected wiring) — **gear
> identity is not the directory registration name** — and the boot mode selects
> which role-qualified name that instance registers under.

The worked case is `event-broker`: boot mode `cluster_dispatcher` registers as
`event-broker` and is the front door; `cluster_ingest` as `event-broker-ingest`,
carrying a `shard` label; `cluster_delivery` as `event-broker-delivery`. A
bare-name resolve reaches only the dispatcher, and the ADR is precise about why
that is worth having: *"not by a filter that could be misconfigured, but because
internal roles were never registered under that name. A forgotten flag cannot
misroute, because there is no flag."*

Two axes, deliberately separated: *"role selects the name, label selects the
instance within it"*. This ADR takes the naming half.

**The ADR says "manifest-declared" six times and never once says what a manifest
is.** No key, no file, no format. That is not an omission in a document this
careful — ADR-0009 owns the runtime's half and correctly declines to invent a
description language it does not own. The open half is a composition-time
declaration, and composition-time declarations are what this tool makes.

### The slot already exists, and ADR-0002 already filed it

`gear_globals` offers `role(name, directory_name, sharded, instance_addressable)`
with its own comment — *"accepted for forward compatibility, excluded from
resolution. The runtime has no role concept."* It lowers to `DeclaredRole`,
rides on `GearDescriptor.declared_roles`, is answered by `declares_unsupported`
and `declares_shards`, exports to TypeScript as `DeclaredRole.ts`, and appears
in `GEAR_FUNCTIONS` so the editor already colours it. The platform's own GDL
reference documents it.

ADR-0002's authority table already puts `declared_roles` in the column for facts
declared in `gear.gdl` because no Rust attribute owns them, with the
justification *"forward compatibility and an opaque pointer"*. That row has
already been revisited once and survived: the 2026-09-04 amendment moved
`config_schema`'s fields to the projected column and said of its neighbour, in
as many words, *"For `declared_roles` that still holds."*

**This decision does not move the row either. It replaces the justification**:
forward compatibility for nothing in particular becomes the manifest that
another repository's accepted ADR requires and does not define.

Nothing uses it. Zero of the corpus's eighteen `gear.gdl` files declares a role,
and `event-broker` — the gear ADR-0009 is written about — has no `gear.gdl` at
all. So the signature is free to change today and will not be free later.

### The evidence points at the wrong repository

`report_role_gaps` in `merge.rs` raises `GBX0601`, whose message says the
runtime *"takes a worker's directory identity from a name fixed in its binary,
with no configuration override"*, citing
`libs/toolkit/src/bootstrap/oop.rs (OopRunOptions.gear_name)`. Every clause is
checkable and the citation does not support the conclusion.

* **The runtime does not constrain the name.** `OopRunOptions.gear_name` is a
  plain `String` with no validator between it and the registration. It takes any
  string offered.
* **"Fixed in its binary" is true, and Gearbox is what fixes it.** `generate/rust.rs`
  passes `gear_name => application.anchor.as_str()` into `worker_main.rs.jinja`,
  which emits `gear_name: "…".to_owned()`. The template's own comment already
  admits the causality: *"The directory identity, verbatim. The runtime takes it
  from this field with no configuration override, **which is why the lock records
  the anchor rather than deriving a name here**."* The name is fixed in the binary
  because we wrote a literal into it.
* **The model conflates two facts into one field.** `ResolvedApplication.anchor`
  is both the gear whose co-location closure defines the application *and* the
  worker's directory identity. There is no `directory_name` for it to be
  anything else, and the field's own doc comment states the false reason in this
  repository's source: *"which is why roles cannot be expressed."*
* **The binding constraint is a cardinality rule in the resolver.** `split` in
  `resolve/partition.rs` looks a pin up with `find`, not `filter`: a second
  `ApplicationPin` on the same anchor is silently dropped. One gear yields one
  application, therefore one binary, therefore one directory name.

> **One gear → N role-named workloads is unexpressible because Gearbox builds
> one application per anchor gear, not because the runtime refuses a name.**

ADR-0009 requires the opposite for Kubernetes — *"each role-name maps to its own
Service"* — so the requirement and the limitation are both ours to reconcile.

Two facts make the correction unarguable. **The boot mode needs no new
mechanism**: `event-broker`'s `DeploymentMode` is an ordinary `serde` enum read
from its config, exactly the shape Gearbox projects as `ConfigFieldType::Enum`
and `use_gear(config = {...})` already writes and checks. What is missing is a
second application to put a second value in — the same cardinality rule, wearing
a different hat. And **the second axis is blocked from our side too**:
`WorkerServe` carries no labels and `OopHttpSection` emits three keys, so
Gearbox cannot write `oop_http.labels` even though the runtime reads it.

### Why the citation cannot simply be reworded

The obvious repair is not available, and the reason it is not available is the
reason the misclassification was findable at all.

A code's domain is a function of its number: `GBX06xx` is `RuntimeGap`.
`every_runtime_gap_code_requires_evidence` asserts that every code in that
domain requires evidence, and `cpt-gearbox-nfr-evidence-cited` requires that
evidence to be a file and line **in `gears-rust`**. A limitation on our side of
the boundary has no such line. The requirement did its job: it demanded a
citation, the only citation available was a plain `String` field, and the
mismatch is the finding. To stop claiming a runtime limitation, the code has to
leave the runtime-gap range.

> **Citations here name functions and types, not line ranges**, following
> ADR-0018. A document about a citation that misleads should not add more of
> them, and line numbers are the part that rots first.

## Decision Outcome

### 1. `role(...)` in `gear.gdl` is the manifest ADR-0009 leaves undefined

A role is a string that names a directory registration. `gear.gdl` is the only
file in either repository that declares composition-time facts about a gear with
no Rust home, and ADR-0002 has already filed roles there. The correspondence:

| ADR-0009 | `gear.gdl` |
|---|---|
| the differentiated mode a gear runs in | `role(name = ...)` |
| the role-qualified directory name it registers under | `role(directory_name = ...)` |
| the front door — bare name, edge-eligible | the role whose `directory_name` is the gear's own id |
| the `shard` label an ingest instance carries | `role(labels = ["shard"])`, see (2) |
| "the boot mode selects which role-qualified name" | the gear's own config enum, set by `use_gear(config = {...})` |

Recorded on ADR-0009 as an amendment rather than a divergence, in the form
ADR-0014 used for the Profile-2 rename: that ADR is accepted, and a second
document defining its undefined half must extend it, not compete with it.

The correspondence imports a constraint, and it becomes ours to enforce:
**instances registered under one directory name must expose the same logical
public API** — a directory name is one logical service. See (3).

### 2. The signature changes while it is free

* **`sharded` and `instance_addressable` become `labels = [...]`.** Two booleans
  cannot say *which* key, and the key is what the runtime needs: `oop_http.labels`
  is a map, matched by `LabelSelector`'s equality-AND semantics. `sharded = True`
  is `labels = ["shard"]` and says strictly more. The gear declares which keys it
  registers under; the values are per-instance and belong to the deployment — the
  runtime's own config doc names the mechanism, a `StatefulSet` ordinal injected
  as `APP__OOP_HTTP__LABELS__SHARD=7`.
* **`directory_name` gets a default and a front-door rule.** Default
  `<gear-id>-<name>`. The front door is the role that sets `directory_name` to
  the gear's own id; at most one may, and two is a refusal. Without that rule
  ADR-0009's structural guarantee does not hold, because nothing says which role
  owns the bare name. No identifier work is required: `GearId` and
  `ApplicationId` share `validate_kebab`, and `event-broker-ingest` is valid in
  both.
* **`name` is defined as the value the gear's own mode selector accepts** — for
  `event-broker`, one of its `DeploymentMode` variants. That is the only spelling
  checkable against a projected enum, and it removes the ambiguity in ADR-0009's
  worked table, whose left column is a mode and right column a name.
* **`replicas` is not added.** It already lives on `ApplicationPin`, which is
  `product.gdl`'s, and that is correct: how many copies of a role run is an
  operator's decision, not a fact about the gear. The product's half of the join
  is one pin per role.

This is the division the `feature("k8s-auth", kinds = ["kubernetes"])` precedent
established and ADR-0014's amendment blessed: the gear declares a true thing
about itself, the product chooses, and the resolver reports contradictions
without ever branching on a kind.

### 3. A role's contracts are projected, not declared

The expected answer here is wrong, in an interesting direction.

**`#[toolkit::contract]` needs nothing, and neither does `#[toolkit::consumes]`.**
Both already carry the gear name as a free string that is used directly as a
directory key. `ContractAttr.gear` is unvalidated and flows verbatim into
`ContractDescriptor.gear`; `ConsumesAttr.from` is emitted verbatim as
`dep_gear`, and the macro crate's own test pins it with the comment *"`from` is
a directory lookup key and must survive untouched."* A role-qualified
`gear = "event-broker-ingest"` is writable in the attribute today.

**And that is exactly why `role(...)` must not grow a contract list.** ADR-0002
forbids a description from restating what a Rust attribute owns, and `GBX0210`
is the active refusal that keeps the decision alive. A role's contract surface
is projected: a contract whose `#[toolkit::contract(gear = ...)]` names a role's
`directory_name` belongs to that role. GDL declares the role's name, Rust
declares which contracts answer to it, and the join is the string. This applies
ADR-0002 rather than bending it — the same correction ADR-0018 made to its own
first draft, and for the same reason: a hand-written list drifts, a projection
cannot.

Where a role dimension *is* genuinely needed is here: `ProviderDescriptor` is
keyed on `provider_gear`, so two roles of one gear providing two contracts are
two providers with one key. That is the one schema change this decision forces.

**Three defects follow, and they are present-tense.** They misfire the moment
any gear writes a role-qualified `gear = "..."` in Rust, whether or not a
`gear.gdl` declares a role:

* **A contract's owner is never checked against the catalogue.** `merge.rs` takes
  it from the attribute by two paths — one falls back to the declaring gear on a
  parse failure, the other diagnoses one — and both guard a *malformed* id.
  `event-broker-ingest` is valid kebab, so it passes either, and the owner then
  names a gear the catalogue does not hold. `GBX0301` would be the code for that,
  and it is raised for `use_gear`, for a plugin under a host, and for a `deps`
  entry — never for a contract owner.
* `merge_contracts` in `catalogue.rs` decides "is this the owner's complete copy"
  by comparing the contract's owner to the declaring gear's id. A role-qualified
  owner never matches, so the provider's full descriptor — the one carrying the
  transport projections — is treated as a consumer's partial restatement and can
  lose to another. A silent wrong merge, not an error.
* `static_endpoint_source` in `resolve/bindings.rs` builds the `consumer_wiring`
  override key from the provider's `GearId`, while the runtime reads the key the
  macro emitted from `from`. Role-qualify `from` and the override is written
  where nothing reads it, silently. Two skews hide here and only one is about
  roles: the description's `consume(from_ = ...)` was a second copy of the
  attribute's `from`, and the *selected* provider can differ from the declared
  one whenever `select_provider` falls back. The first is not cross-checked but
  **removed** -- `from_` is refused by `GBX0210` and the attribute projected, so
  there is one copy -- which is what ADR-0002 asks for and what makes the second
  checkable at all. `GBX0206` keeps the half the macro still owns twice: the
  consumer segment, derived from the struct identifier.

One thing does need a `gears-rust` change, and it is not `#[toolkit::contract]`:
ADR-0009 requires role-qualified **gRPC service names**, because
`resolve_grpc_service` is service-name-scoped across all gears and gear-name
isolation does not reach it. That name comes from the gRPC contract and the
proto, which is the platform's surface to shape rather than ours -- so it is
named here as their work rather than designed.

### 4. The boundary is the model, and `GBX0601` moves rather than being reworded

**Retire `GBX0601` and mint a topology code in the `GBX03xx` range.** Leave the
number deliberately absent with a comment saying why, as `GBX0201`–`GBX0205` and
`GBX0605` already are. The domain follows the number, and the claim is not about
the runtime.

The replacement says what is true: a gear declares roles, a product builds one
application per anchor gear, so at most one of them can be deployed. Its help
points at the pin, and its evidence — which a topology code does not require — is
our own source. That absence is the point: the runtime-gap contract forbids
citing ourselves, and the honest citation is ourselves.

**`GBX0602` is a separate correction, and part of its claim has gone false.**
It says instance labels exist only on the out-of-process path and in-process
gears carry none. ADR-0009's Layer 1 has since landed in `gears-rust`:
`ServiceInstanceInfo` and `RegisterInstanceInfo` carry labels, `LabelSelector`
and `resolve_by_labels` exist, `oop_http.labels` is a first-class config field
with environment sourcing, and boot validates it. For Profiles 2 and 3 the
runtime expresses per-instance addressing today. What survives is the Profile-1
half, which is ADR-0009's own stated coverage gap rather than a defect; what
replaces the rest is a statement about us — `WorkerServe` has no labels and
`OopHttpSection` writes three keys, so Gearbox cannot emit one.

`ResolvedApplication.anchor`'s doc comment is corrected in the same breath. A
wrong sentence in a struct's documentation is read by more people than a
diagnostic message.

### 5. Studio learns roles after the signature settles, not before

Studio does not know about roles at all: `DeclaredRole.ts` is generated and
read by nobody, and `declared_roles` is displayed nowhere. Three surfaces are
affected, and the order between them is load-bearing.

* **The New Gear wizard.** `scaffold_gear_files` offers each `GearKind` a block
  of *commented* declarations with prose — that is how `provides`, `consumes`
  and `config_schema` are offered — under the rule `GearKind`'s own comment
  states: *"A scaffold must not produce a description that is already wrong."*
  `roles = [...]` joins that block in the `Service` shape.
* **No fourth `GearKind`.** The corpus decided there are three, and a freshly
  scaffolded gear is single-role by definition. Roles appear when a gear grows a
  second mode, which is an edit to an existing description, not a scaffold.
* **The wizard must not learn `role()` before this ADR settles the signature.**
  A hint written today would teach `sharded` and `instance_addressable` to every
  new gear, in the spelling (2) retires, and a scaffold that mints descriptions
  in a retired spelling is the thing `GearKind`'s rule exists to prevent. The
  order is: this ADR, then `gear_globals`, then the scaffold hint, then the
  Inspector.
* **Round-trip is already safe, and that is a property rather than a
  coincidence.** `edit_call` edits by byte spans from the parser with no
  re-serialisation, so a tier-3 surgical edit under ADR-0010 preserves a
  `roles = [...]` it knows nothing about. Nothing needs fixing; it needs stating,
  so nobody later "adds role support" to the editor and takes the guarantee away.

### 6. Out of scope, each with a reason

* **The shard and label axis.** ADR-0009 splits the axes deliberately; this ADR
  takes the naming half. Writing `oop_http.labels` needs a field on
  `WorkerServe`, one on `OopHttpSection`, a per-instance value source, and a
  Kubernetes workload that is not a single VIP-fronted `Deployment`. That is its
  own decision.
* **Role-qualified gRPC service names** — the platform's own surface, named
  rather than designed.
* **`TopologyView`, ownership assignment and stale-owner fencing** — consumer-gear
  domain logic by ADR-0009's own scoping. Gearbox generates none of it, and
  saying so keeps this ADR from being read later as having promised it.
* **Roles as a scoping dimension.** ADR-0014 parks profiles and says new design
  should assume one profile per product. A role is scoped by the application pin,
  which already carries `profiles`; it must not become a third axis.
* **Embedded.** ADR-0009 states the hole in its own voice — *"one process cannot
  host two instances of a name, nor two role-modes of one gear… a **coverage
  gap** in the ADR-0001 profile matrix"* — and assigns coverage to the adopting
  gear. Our mirror needs no new code: `report_embedded_violations` already
  downgrades every application pin under an embedded profile, and a role-bearing
  pin is one more of those.

## Consequences

* **The Studio surface is three places that know nothing about roles**, and
  ADR-0010 tier 0 raises the cost of the first one: *a preview is not optional*,
  so a role the scaffold can write must be visible in the file plan before
  anything is written. The Inspector and a conformance claim follow.
* **`ResolvedApplication.anchor` stops being two facts.** Either a
  `directory_name` joins it or `anchor` is documented as the closure key alone.
  Either way `LOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` moves, every `lock_hash` moves, and
  `gearbox-lock`'s structural diff gains a field. The doc comment is wrong *now*,
  before any of that.
* **Application naming does a plausible wrong thing under roles.** `derive_name`
  names an application after its anchor and `unique` resolves a collision by
  appending `-2`, so two unpinned roles of one gear produce `event-broker` and
  `event-broker-2` — names that look right and are not the ones ADR-0009
  requires. The dedup path must be unreachable for roles.
* **Relaxing the cardinality rule relaxes a check that catches a real mistake.**
  ADR-0014's groundwork records that `ApplicationPin` does not go through
  `claim()` and duplicates surface only after narrowing. Two pins on one anchor
  is exactly that case. Admitting roles must not silently re-admit an accidental
  duplicate: pins must differ by role, and a pair that does not is still a
  duplicate.
* **Three of the defects in (3) are live today**, triggered by a role-qualified
  `gear = "..."` anywhere in the platform's Rust, with or without a description.
  The platform could introduce one tomorrow and the catalogue would mis-merge
  quietly.
* **Nothing in the corpus can confirm this.** Zero of eighteen descriptions
  declares a role and `event-broker` has none at all, so every confirmation below
  is a fixture until the platform describes it — the same cross-repository
  dependency ADR-0018 named for its four missing descriptions.
* **The generated Kubernetes shape already contradicts ADR-0009**, for every
  worker and before roles exist. `partition.rs` writes the Service VIP into
  `advertise_uri`, and the Helm templates hold a `Deployment` and a `Service`
  with no `StatefulSet` and no headless Service. ADR-0009 mandates no workload
  kind but does say a targeted role-name is *"**never** fronted by a VIP (which
  would defeat targeting)"*. This ADR names that and does not fix it.
* **Nothing reaches the lock yet.** `ResolvedGear` has no role field, so
  `declared_roles` lives in the catalogue and stops there. Recording this
  decision changes no lock byte; *placing* a role does.
* **The Studio types are already built**, and changing the signature regenerates
  three files while breaking no author, because there are no authors.
* **Good: the manifest question closes for both repositories at once.** ADR-0009's
  undefined half gets a key, a file and a format, and a construct that exists
  here only as a promise gets a reason.
* **Good: the correction is portable.** Once "the directory name is a decision
  Gearbox writes" is stated, the same sentence explains the label gap, the VIP
  gap and the config-cardinality gap. Three open items collapse into one rule.

## Confirmation

* **No test asserts that `GBX0601` or `GBX0602` is raised at all**, and saying so
  is part of the correction. `GapRoles` appears as a sorting fixture in
  `gearbox-ir`'s diagnostics tests, and in `gearbox-gdl`'s
  `roles_are_recorded_but_refused_with_cited_evidence`, which asserts that
  *nothing* is raised and defers with *"Gap diagnostics are asserted in
  gearbox-engine"* — where they are not. The one claim this ADR corrects has
  never been under test.
* **The runtime-accepts-any-name claim** is confirmed by generation: a fixture
  whose anchor is role-shaped must emit that string into `worker_main.rs` and
  nothing may reject it.
* **The one-application-per-anchor claim** is confirmed by a fixture with two
  application pins on one anchor. Today exactly one application is built and the
  second pin produces no diagnostic. That test does not exist and should, whether
  or not roles ever land.
* **The test that forecloses the cheap fix must keep passing**:
  `every_runtime_gap_code_requires_evidence`. Rewording `GBX0601` while it stays
  a runtime-gap code is not available, and that test is why.
* **The `consumer_wiring` skew** is confirmed by extending the existing claim
  that a Kubernetes worker wires the provider gear rather than the contract: with
  a role-qualified provider the emitted key must equal the string the macro emits
  as `dep_gear`, and today it does not.
* **The `merge_contracts` defect** is confirmed today with no new feature: a
  fixture whose contract attribute names a gear the catalogue does not hold must
  be reported rather than silently producing a dangling owner.
* **The Embedded refusal needs no new confirmation**, and saying so is the point:
  a role-bearing pin under an embedded profile is already covered by
  `report_embedded_violations`.
* **Determinism must survive N applications per anchor**, which is a new source
  of ordering. The byte-stability claim over shuffled orderings and the
  one-description-three-locks claim are what catch it going non-deterministic.

## Traceability

* **Amends `cpt-cf-adr-instance-addressable-discovery`** (accepted): supplies the
  manifest its modelling rule requires and never defines. Recorded as an
  amendment note on that ADR, in the form ADR-0014 used for the Profile-2 rename.
* **Amends ADR-0002 in its justification only.** `declared_roles` stays in the
  declared column, where that ADR's own 2026-09-04 amendment already re-affirmed
  it while moving `config_schema` out; "forward compatibility" is replaced by the
  real reason. The authority split is **applied rather than bent**: a role's
  contract surface is projected from the contract attribute and never restated in
  `role(...)`.
* **Will retire `GBX0601`** and mint a topology code, leaving the number absent
  with a comment — future tense, deliberately.
* **Will reword `GBX0602`**: the runtime-cannot-express claim is false for
  Profiles 2 and 3 since ADR-0009's Layer 1 landed. What survives is Profile 1,
  which is ADR-0009's own gap, and our inability to emit `oop_http.labels`.
* **Corrects a doc comment, not only a diagnostic**: `ResolvedApplication.anchor`
  states the false reason in this repository's own source. That correction lands
  with this ADR; the diagnostic move does not.
* **Follows the `feature(kinds = [...])` precedent** and ADR-0014's amendment
  blessing the gear→kind direction: the gear declares a fact about itself, the
  product decides, the resolver reports contradictions and never branches.
* **References ADR-0016** for the application vocabulary this keys on, **ADR-0018**
  for the projection-over-restatement correction it reuses, **ADR-0010** for the
  tier rules the scaffold and the surgical editor answer to, and **ADR-0015** for
  why the evidence contract exists and why it is what exposed this.
* **Names, rather than designs, two pieces of the platform's own work**: the
  role-qualified gRPC service-name requirement, and `event-broker`'s missing
  `gear.gdl`. Both are shapes that repository owns. This is not a claim that
  `gears-rust` cannot be written to -- ADR-0010 argues the opposite, that a ban
  by location is the wrong boundary and ownership is the right one.
* Related requirements: `cpt-gearbox-fr-gdl-no-restatement`,
  `cpt-gearbox-nfr-evidence-cited`.
* **Does not decide** the shard and label axis, the Kubernetes workload shape, or
  per-instance label sourcing. Named, scoped out, and left with reasons.
